episode.title: Jam Day Under the Baobab
episode.theme: Lebo and Jabu turn a berry-jam mess into a picnic under a baobab.
learning: Notice that baobabs are remarkable trees found in parts of Africa
See how friends can solve a messy problem together

scenes.action: Lebo races into a sunny clearing and stops in amazement at a huge baobab. Jabu trots in behind her and nearly bumps into her.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Whoa! Jabu, look at that tree! Its tummy is bigger than yours!

dialogue.speaker: Jabu
dialogue.text: Prrr-ooo?
dialogue.performance: elephant vocalisation; no human-language dubbing required

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Okay, okay. Maybe not bigger. But why is the trunk so wide?

shots.action: Establish clearing, baobab and birds; Lebo runs in.
Lebo points up; Jabu arrives and reacts.
Lebo compares the trunk to Jabu; playful reaction.
They circle the trunk and decide to picnic nearby.

culturalNotes: The baobab is a real tree, not a magical stereotype. Avoid assigning a specific cultural meaning without a sourced regional review.

scenes.action: They collect berries and simple picnic ingredients. Lebo turns collecting into a counting game.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: We need berries for our jam. One basket for us, and one little bowl to share.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Let’s count together. One, two, three, four, five!

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Jabu, your trunk is the fastest berry-picker I’ve ever seen.

dialogue.speaker: Jabu
dialogue.text: Prrrp!

shots.action: They walk beside the clearing, spotting berries.
Count five safe, generic berries into a basket.
Jabu carefully picks with trunk, then poses proudly.
They return to the picnic table with baskets.

scenes.action: Lebo explains the order: bowl, berries, mash, stir. Jabu tries to help, sneezes, and sends berries bouncing everywhere.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: First, bowl. Then berries. Then mash. Then stir. In that order!

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Ready, Jabu? Gently does it.

dialogue.speaker: Jabu
dialogue.text: Prrr... prrr... PAA-CHOO!

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: The berries are escaping!

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Catch the purple one! No, the other purple one!

shots.action: Show four-step sequence with bowl and spoon.
Jabu leans in carefully; nose tickles.
Sneeze build-up.
Berry bounce chaos across table and grass.
Lebo and Jabu chase rolling berries without panic.

scenes.action: They stop, assess the mess, clean what can safely be cleaned, and start again with a smaller batch. The lesson is cooperation, not perfection.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Well... that did not go to plan.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: But we can fix it. We’ll pick up, clean up, and try again.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: You gather. I sort. Then we both stir.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Look! A small pot of jam and a very big adventure.

dialogue.speaker: Jabu
dialogue.text: Prrr-ooo!

shots.action: Quiet beat; they look at the mess.
Team clean-up and sorting.
Restart with a small clean batch; mash and stir.
They taste a tiny spoonful safely.
Lay out the picnic and celebrate teamwork.

culturalNotes: Food remains generic in this version. Region-specific preparation should only be added after cultural review.

scenes.action: They sit under the tree. Lebo gives the recurring fact segment, then they invite children to keep exploring Africa.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Jabu’s Africa Fact!

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Baobabs grow in several parts of Africa. Their thick trunks can store lots of water, which helps them through dry times.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Africa is full of different places, people, plants and stories. We’ll discover another one next time.

dialogue.speaker: Lebo
dialogue.text: Bye, explorers!

dialogue.speaker: Jabu
dialogue.text: Prrr-oooo!

shots.action: Golden light under baobab.
Jabu’s Africa Fact.
Simple Africa silhouette with varied landscapes; no national stereotypes.
Lebo waves; Jabu trumpets; end card.

culturalNotes: Final fact wording must be independently reviewed before the episode is called fact-locked.

factNotes: Keep the baobab fact general: baobabs grow naturally in several parts of Africa.
Do not present one food tradition as representative of all African communities.
Any later local-language words or region-specific customs require a reviewer from that language/cultural context.

musicDirection.theme: Bright, playful, acoustic African-inspired children’s theme using original melodies only.
musicDirection.rule: Do not imitate or interpolate an existing children's song or soundtrack.
